text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Miners in the Motru coalfield oppose privatisation of the sector.
- Lack of orders forced Roman SA truck maker in Brasov to stop production for one week.
- Commercial banks will give the farm sector credits worth 550 billion lei to start seasonal works.
- Romania and Ukraine will resume negociations on a bilateral treaty.
- The newspaper publishes the indictment against miners' union leader Miron Cosma related to riots which toppled Romania's first post-communist government in 1991.
- A full-page report outlines activities of the Romanian Foreign Intelligence Service and alleges they were "mafia-like".
- Greece will support Romania's bid to join NATO, said Defence Minister Victor Babiuc after meeting his Greek counterpart.
- Unknown persons kidnapped a 12-year old child in the northeastern city of Iasi and asked for a 100 million lei ransom.

- The newspaper quotes William Roth, Chairman of the North Atlantic Assembly, as saying that NATO's aim is to integrate in its structures new democracies from Central Europe like Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary and Slovenia. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
